verdict.rationale: Muse runs on its own VM with a file system and terminal. Its docs state that everything Muse generates is stored there and that users can inspect, edit and download those files. It can also build artifacts like trackers, study guides and dashboards. Nothing in the pack specifically mentions documents or presentations, or shows the assistant revising files over multiple turns. missing for 10: explicit document/presentation creation, assistant-driven iterative editing, export format details, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a knowledge-worker, I can have the assistant create and iteratively edit documents, presentations, and other files I can export

citations.quote: All the files you put in your VM and everything Muse generates or uses on your behalf is stored there. You can inspect, edit and download these files freely
Muse has its own computer, with a file system and a terminal, so it can write its own code and build the tools a task needs.
It can build a tracker for your spending, an interactive study guide, or a dashboard to find patterns in your sleep.
